en: When PAGASA reports a heat index above 42°C, you should avoid outdoor play to prevent dangerous heatstroke.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground, taking cover under a sturdy desk, and holding on protects you from falling debris.
Floodwaters from the water cycle can carry rat urine containing Leptospira bacteria, so you must wash your legs with soap after wading.
Looking directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses can permanently damage your retina, even during a partial solar eclipse.
During a spring tide caused by the aligned sun and moon, unusually strong ocean currents can easily sweep wading children out to sea.
Soil can harbor hookworm larvae that penetrate bare skin, so wearing shoes while playing outside prevents painful intestinal infections.
Fine volcanic ash contains tiny rock particles that can irritate your lungs, so wearing an N95 mask during ashfall protects your breathing.
A Public Storm Warning Signal number one means winds of 39 to 61 kilometers per hour are expected, so you must secure loose roof sheets.
The water cycle distributes fresh water, but you must always boil river or well water for at least one minute to kill disease-causing microorganisms.
The sun emits ultraviolet radiation that causes sunburn, so applying sunscreen with SPF 30 before recess protects your skin from cellular damage.
If the ocean water suddenly recedes far from the shore before a tsunami, you must immediately walk to higher ground instead of watching.
Climate change increases heavy rainfall that fills empty tires with stagnant water, creating perfect breeding grounds for dengue-carrying Aedes mosquitoes.
